chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Hamzah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who hires a beast of burden and says, 'I have hired it from you to such and such a place.' If it exceeds that place by a certain amount and he names that excess, he said, 'There is no objection to all of it.'

key_terms.إِلَى مَكَانٍ كَذَا: to such and such a place

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a hired animal travels further than the agreed destination?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of the ijarah contract in Shia jurisprudence, specifically addressing the scenario where an animal exceeds the agreed-upon destination by a specified margin. It establishes that such deviation does not invalidate the contract, reflecting the principle of ease in commercial transactions. This ruling is foundational in the chapter on leases (Bab al-Ijarat) within Shaykh al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam, demonstrating the practical application of contractual validity in early Islamic trade.
